messages:
Eli: Heads-up: we're validating cutover options. Two competing ideas: lease-based demotion (give old region a short lease to accept writes) vs proxy-side buffering (API gateway holds writes and forwards after migration). Thoughts?

Rhea: Lease-based seems simpler for runtime but worries about cross-region transfer for EU tenants (legal). We need a consent check before any cross-border transfer.

Sam: Proxy buffering keeps legal boundaries clearer (gateway can enforce region), but adds load and tail-latency at the edge. Also more complex retries if gateway restarts.

Priya: Idea: hybrid model. Gateway opts to buffer only idempotent ops or small payloads; heavy payloads get immediate 409 with retry instructions. Buffer TTL = 45s by default.

Eli: Agree hybrid makes sense. Operational questions: where do we keep the buffer? In-memory at gateway (fast) or backed by local durable queue (safer)?

Rhea: For safety prefer local durable queue (SQS/Kafka) + compacting by idempotency-key. But that increases cost and complexity. Could we do ephemeral in-memory with a synchronous replicate-to-queue fallback when threshold exceeded?

Sam: We also need to standardize client behavior. Suggest adding `X-Redwood-Cutover-Mode` header so clients can opt-in to server buffering vs failing-fast. Default server behavior = fail-fast for non-idempotent writes.

Priya: Example header usage:

```
POST /v1/items
Idempotency-Key: abc-123
X-Redwood-Cutover-Mode: buffer-if-allowed
```

Gateway checks tenant consent flag before sending across regions. If consent=false && target-region!=origin, gateway returns 451 or 409 depending on route.

Eli: Lease demotion sketch: old primary holds a short lease (e.g., 25s) during cutover. It will accept writes and mark them `lease_handoff=true` then replicate with priority. Reads during lease: read-from-primary if `read_consistent=true` or `prefer-local` otherwise.

Rhea: Concern: KV cache contamination. If local caches serve stale state after handoff, clients can observe false positives. Need to invalidate or attach `valid_after` metadata.

Sam: Add a `handoff_token` concept similar to existing ideas. Token issued by control-plane at cutover start, expires with lease. Clients/gateways include it so runtime can return `stale_ok` flags and serve conditional reads.

Priya: Ops safety valve: if replication lag > 2x expected or backlog > 3k ops, control-plane toggles tenant into `reject` mode and drains buffers with best-effort. Also surface a tenant-level incident.

infra-bot: Ticket infra/cutover-handoff #901 created: track buffer durability experiment + legal gating tests.

Eli: Metrics to add: buffer_size_bytes, buffered_requests_count, handoff_accepted/s, handoff_replicated/s, buffer_drops/s, buffer_replay_errors/s. Also tracing span linking gateway buffer -> runtime replicate -> primary ack.

Rhea: For EU contracts: we'll add an auditable log entry for any cross-region transfer with tenant consent flag, timestamp, and dataset hash. That should help compliance reviews.

Sam: Small perf note: proxy buffering will add a P99 tail depending on queue ack. We'll run a canary with 500 rps and 1MB/req payloads to measure.

Priya: I'll draft the state machine and a short API change doc for X-Redwood-Cutover-Mode and handoff_token by EOD. Eli, can you own the perf canary?

Eli: Yep, I'll run canary tomorrow and post results. Meeting to finalize RFC Friday 9am PT. :+1:
